newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.banker not worried by big zloty swings.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.banker not worried by big zloty swings.

text.p: Polish central bank chief said on Thursday she was not worried by the recent steep zloty fall as depleted foreign investor portfolios in the region left little downside for the local currency.
Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz also told Reuters in an interview that the bank believed bigger zloty swings within the 14-percent daily trading band were acceptable.
The zloty slid five percent on Tuesday against a basket of foreign currencies. After partial recovery and stabilisation on Wednesday, it showed signs of nervousness again on Thursday.
"The current zloty level reflects the widening trade deficit, certain risks relating to the upcoming elections and a certain regional risk," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
"But nervous reactions are unfounded because that is why we have a trading band of seven percent above and below (the central parity) for the zloty to fluctuate within this range." she added.

She said the central bank, which until recently has been limiting the zloty's movements to cap its appreciation, agreed with recent International Monetary Fund suggestions the zloty should be allowed to float more freely within its trading band.
"The IMF recommended that the exchange rate should be more flexible and we believe it is justified," she said.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the bank saw little further risk for the zloty and was confident a widening of the trading band would not be necessary.
"Because investors have left the region following the Czech crisis there is no substantial risk for the zloty," she said. @
Asked whether the bank would consider widening the trading band if the zloty fell again under pressure Gronkiewicz-Waltz said: "I believe that there will be no such need."
